title: Quantum holography and associative chiral Koszul duality
subtitle: Ordered collisions, chiral quantum groups, and the relation between boundary operators and bulk theories.
lead: This programme studies singular composition with the order of the inputs retained. Its objects include vertex and quantum vertex algebras, differential-module coefficients on configurations of points, and categories of modules with fusion and exchange. The question is associative: it concerns multiplication and modules before passage to a commutator. Lie–commutative chiral Koszul duality supplies enveloping examples; an associative dual must also carry ordered products and their higher coherences.

The geometric construction separates collision from cutting a configuration into disjoint consecutive blocks. Bar and cobar relate multiplication to coherent comultiplication in this setting. Realizing a dual by fields asks for further structure across the collision diagonals, and scalar terms in the original relations can become curvature. The coefficient category, completion, empty unit and local vacuum are part of the mathematical data.

A chiral quantum group should describe how modules combine and exchange as their insertion points move. A coproduct that adds levels, a map that adds ranks, and fusion within one fixed-level category have different domains. Comparing them requires a functor with a tensorator, a parameter map and coherent unit laws.

Holography as Koszul duality asks for comparisons with an independently defined bulk theory: its boundary operators, its lines as modules of a dual algebra, their endpoint couplings and fusion, and its local operations. Supported abelian constructions give concrete examples of these comparisons. A joint nonabelian theorem remains open, and preparing a state from a gravitational bulk requires additional amplitudes and sewing data.

principal.title: Associative bar–cobar duality with finite arity filtrations
principal.text: Let \(X\) be a smooth separated finite-type curve over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), and equip \(\mathcal S_X=D(k)\times\prod_{n\geq1}\operatorname{DMod}(X^n)\) with consecutive-cut convolution, using unbounded right algebraic differential modules with quasi-coherent underlying modules and derived external tensors. Bar and cobar give inverse equivalences between augmented coherent associative algebras with \(A_0\simeq k\) and counital coaugmented coherent coassociative coalgebras with \(C_0\simeq k\), including mapping spaces; each reduced word at arity \(n\) has length at most \(n\), so no cohomological boundedness assumption is needed. These equivalences restrict to algebras whose positive-arity coefficients vanish on every separated cut and strong cut coalgebras. For such a coalgebra, \(\overline{\Omega C}_n\simeq R\Gamma_{Z_n}(C_n)[-1]\), where \(Z_1=X\) and \(Z_n=\bigcap_{p=1}^{n-1}\bigcup_{i\leq p<j}\Delta_{ij}\) for \(n\geq2\); in particular, \(Z_3=\Delta_{13}\).

principal.title: Curved duality for universal affine and Virasoro modes
principal.text: Over discrete \(\mathbb C\), take the universal affine algebra of a finite-dimensional simple \(\mathfrak g\), with \(\operatorname{Kill}=2h^\vee(\ ,\ )\), at any level \(\kappa\), or the universal Virasoro algebra at any charge \(c\), in a fixed formal coordinate. For \(\mathfrak t=\mathfrak g((z))\) or \(\mathbb C((z))\partial_z\), with \(L_n=-z^{n+1}\partial_z\), choose the positive subalgebra \(\mathfrak p=\mathfrak g[[z]]\) or \(\prod_{n\geq0}\mathbb C L_n\), respectively, and exhaust its discrete complement by finite-dimensional spaces \(D_m\); the curved ghost algebra is \(B_\eta=\varprojlim_m(\Lambda\mathfrak p^\vee\otimes\Lambda D_m^*,d_{\rm CE},+\eta)\), with \(\eta(xz^m,yz^n)=\kappa m(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0}\) or \(\eta(L_m,L_n)=c(m^3-m)\delta_{m+n,0}/12\), and the limit is degreewise, with finite positive support allowed to vary with the negative-mode subset and no product over exterior degrees. Smoothness means that each vector is killed by some positive-mode tail; smooth complexes modulo those coacyclic on \(\mathfrak p\) are equivalent to graded-projective curved \(B_\eta\)-contramodules modulo those with Becker-coacyclic positive quotient; passing to ordinary derived smooth modules requires the further quotient by objects whose inverse image is acyclic. Complementary categorical duality has parameters \(-\kappa-2h^\vee\) and \(26-c\), including critical level, while the algebraic dual is the curved ghost algebra just described; simple integrable and minimal-model quotients are outside this theorem.

principal.title: The spectral bar comparison on augmentation-generated categories
principal.text: Let \(H\) be an augmented dg bialgebra over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), with strict dg coproduct and a degree-zero locally nilpotent algebra derivation and coalgebra coderivation \(T\) satisfying \([d_H,T]=0\) and \(\varepsilon T=0\). Use the direct-sum normalized bar resolution, full-product Hom cochains \(C(M)=R\operatorname{Hom}_H(k,M)\), and \(B=C(k)\); for \(s\in k\), the translated coproduct \(\Delta_s=(e^{sT}\otimes1)\Delta\) gives a natural comparison \(C(M)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}{}_{\Theta_s}C(N)\longrightarrow C(M\otimes_sN)\), where \(\Theta_s\) translates the bar inputs and twists the second left \(B\)-action. This map is an equivalence whenever either input belongs to \(\operatorname{thick}(k)\subset D(H)\), and cochains identify \(\operatorname{thick}(k)\) with \(\operatorname{Perf}(B)\), with coherent translated products and units. If the augmentation module \(k\) is compact in \(D(H)\), the equivalence extends to \(\operatorname{Loc}(k)\simeq D(B)\); compactness alone does not make \(k\) generate all of \(D(H)\).

principal.title: Formal higher cohomology on the Hilbert scheme
principal.text: For \(N\geq1\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex-superalgebra sheaf obtained by framed \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) BRST reduction of adjoint and fundamental symplectic bosons with fundamental fermions on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\), over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\): each of \(\mathcal D\) and \(\mathcal D/\hbar^m\mathcal D\), \(m\geq1\), has nonzero sheaf cohomology exactly in degrees \(0,\ldots,N-1\). For \(N\geq2\), its normal-cup subalgebra generated by the vacuum and translated determinant classes is \((R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Lambda(e_0,e_1,\ldots))/(\hbar e_r,\Lambda^{\geq N})\), with only finite sums and products in the generators. Here \(e_r\) has sheaf degree one, intrinsic even parity and conformal weight \(r+1\); increasing products of fewer than \(N\) generators are nonzero, not \(\hbar\)-divisible, and have independent nonzero images in every finite \(\hbar\) quotient. These positive-degree classes vanish after taking the torus-finite part and then specializing \(\hbar=1\).

principal.title: Minimal-model fusion with a finite-base fibre
principal.text: Let \(2\leq p<q\) be coprime, set \(c_{p,q}=1-6(p-q)^2/(pq)\), and let \(\mathcal C_{p,q}\) be the complex linear category of finite direct sums of simple \(L(c_{p,q},0)\)-modules, with the simple vacuum as tensor unit. If \(I\) indexes its simple modules, the functor \(F(M)=\bigoplus_{i,j\in I}\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,M\boxtimes L_j)\) is exact, faithful and strong monoidal into finite \(\mathbb C^I\)-bimodules, using tensor product over \(\mathbb C^I\). The finite weak Hopf algebra \(H=\bigoplus_{a\in I}\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(F(L_a))\) reconstructs the ribbon category and its full rational Ward output, with module tensor product \(\Delta(1)(V\otimes W)\), where \(\Delta(1)\) projects onto matching intermediate labels. Its canonical finite pairing tensor satisfies both coproduct pairing laws and the categorical exchange identity; its scalar counit need not be multiplicative.

principal.title: Abelian bulk sources give full boundary Fock modules
principal.text: On \(M=\mathbb C_z\times\mathbb R_{\geq0}\), oriented by \(dx\wedge dy\wedge dt\), fix \(\kappa\in\mathbb C^\times\) and let \(A(U)\) be compactly supported differential forms whose boundary pullback lies in \(dz\wedge\Omega_c^\bullet(U\cap\partial M)\). The Gaussian observables \(\bigoplus_{m\geq0}\operatorname{Sym}_b^m(A(U)[2])\) use completed projective bornological tensors at each field number, an algebraic sum over field numbers, and the BV pairing \(-\kappa(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_U a\wedge b\). For a proper vertical ray \(L\) beginning at the boundary and charge \(\alpha\in\mathbb C\), the supported source differential is \(d+\Delta_\kappa-i\alpha I_L\), where \(I_L(a)=\int_La\) on spatial one-forms and is zero on other linear degrees; its rotation-finite endpoint cohomology is concentrated in degree zero and equals \(\mathcal F_\alpha=\mathbb C[J_{-1},J_{-2},\ldots]|\alpha\rangle\). The complete current action is \(J_{-n}=x_n\), \(J_n=\kappa n\partial_{x_n}\) for \(n>0\), and \(J_0=\alpha\), on algebraic polynomial states.

statements.title: A free field with two independent parameters
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\kappa,\lambda\in\mathbb C\) and give \(V=\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), \(Tx_r=rx_{r+1}\), the Wick contraction \(P(u)=\kappa u^{-2}+\lambda u^{-1}\). Its exchange satisfies \(S(u)(x_1\otimes x_1)=x_1\otimes x_1-2\lambda u^{-1}1\otimes1\), and its ordinary unital geometric point modules with all marked collisions are exactly the smooth modules with \([J_m,J_n]=(\kappa m\delta_{m+n,0}+\lambda\varepsilon(m)\delta_{m+n,-1})1\), where \(\varepsilon(m)=1\) for \(m\ge0\) and \(-1\) otherwise. The curved dual has zero differential and curvature \(\sum_{r\ge1}(\kappa r e_r+\lambda e_{r-1})e_{-r}\) on exterior cochains completed by finite negative-mode cutoffs separately in each exterior degree, with finite positive-mode support at each cutoff. For any two contractions of this form, the primitive field map \(V_{P+Q}\to V_P\otimes V_Q\) preserves fields and exchange and adds the contraction parameters; it is not a fixed-level fusion coproduct.

statements.title: Fock modules and rational coinvariants
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), consider Heisenberg modules with \([a_m,a_n]=m\kappa\delta_{m+n,0}\), each positive mode locally nilpotent, and sufficiently high positive modes annihilating each vector. The assignment \(E\mapsto\mathcal F(E)=E[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\), with \(a_{-m}=x_m\), \(a_m=m\kappa\partial_{x_m}\) and \(a_0=A_E\), is an exact equivalence from \(\mathbb C[a_0]\)-modules, and negative-current coinvariants recover \(E\). At finitely many distinct complex points, the derived coinvariants of the algebraic tensor product of these Fock modules under rational currents vanishing at infinity are \(\bigotimes_iE_i\) in degree zero. For finite-dimensional \(E_i\), their coinvariant connection is \(d+\kappa^{-1}\sum_{i<j}A_iA_j\,d\log(p_i-p_j)\); on scalar-charge dual fibres the positive half-exchange is \(e^{\pi i\alpha\beta/\kappa}\) followed by the flip, with normalized associator equal to one.

statements.title: Grading changes the derived endomorphisms
statements.text: For the algebraic Heisenberg mode algebra \(A_\kappa\) over \(\mathbb C\), with \(\kappa\ne0\), put \(\mathfrak n_-=\bigoplus_{m\ge1}\mathbb Ca_{-m}\), \(W=A_\kappa\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n_-)}\mathbb C\) and \(R=\mathbb C[a_0]\). With \(\deg a_n=n\), internally graded derived Hom, summed over internal degrees but retaining full products within each homogeneous component, gives a formal endomorphism dg algebra with value \(R\). In the ordinary unbounded derived category of all algebraic \(A_\kappa\)-modules, \(\operatorname{Ext}^0(W,W)=R\), \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(W,W)=(\prod_{m\ge1}V_m)/(\bigoplus_{m\ge1}V_m)\), where \(V_m=a_mR[a_m,a_{m+1},\ldots]\), and every other degree vanishes. For every polynomial Fock module \(\mathcal F(E)\), full \(\operatorname{RHom}(W,\mathcal F(E))\) vanishes, whereas derived negative-current coinvariants equal \(E[0]\).

statements.title: The Gaussian bulk and its boundary current
statements.text: On \(\mathbb C\times\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), take the Gaussian abelian Chern–Simons observable complex over \(\mathbb C\), with numerical \(k=\hbar\kappa\ne0\), pairing \(-\kappa(2\pi i)^{-1}\int\alpha\wedge\beta\), and boundary condition \(j^*\alpha\in dz\wedge\Omega_c^\bullet\). Its carrier is the direct sum over field number of completed projective bornological symmetric powers, realized by compact smooth kernels satisfying that boundary condition in every variable. The rotation-finite boundary cohomology is the universal rank-one Heisenberg vertex algebra \(V_k\), while interior cohomology is an exterior algebra on one degree-one class. With orientation \(dx\wedge dy\wedge dt\), the outward-oriented sphere operation and the generator \(\xi\) normalized by \(\iota_{J_0}\xi=1\), the bulk bracket is \(\{\xi,\xi\}=2\pi i/k\), and the corresponding finite-jet vacuum cohomology has algebraic secondary pairing \(1/k\).

statements.title: Vacuum extensions detect the Heisenberg level
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\) at \(\kappa\ne0\), restrict the polynomial Heisenberg Fock construction to finite-dimensional \(\mathbb C[t]\)-modules with nilpotent \(t\), where \(a_0=t\), and transport the product by \(\mathcal F(M)\star\mathcal F(N)=\mathcal F(M\otimes N)\). Prescribe the conformal-block connection \(d-(T_M\otimes T_N/\kappa)\,dz/z\) on these chosen coefficient spaces, with the ordinary associator; the positive half-exchange is \(\operatorname{flip}\exp(\pi iT_M\otimes T_N/\kappa)\). On the marked vacuum extension \(J=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), with its inclusion and quotient maps \(i:\mathbb C\to J\), \(p:J\to\mathbb C\), normalized by \(i(1)=t\), \(p(1)=1\), \(p(t)=0\), and \(n=ip\), positive pure braid is \(1+(2\pi i/\kappa)n\otimes n\). A complex-linear exact strong braided equivalence preserving this exact marked extension and its unit identification between levels \(\kappa,\kappa'\ne0\) therefore requires \(\kappa=\kappa'\), although the ambient associative algebra \(\operatorname{RHom}_{\mathbb C[t]}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)\simeq\Lambda(\epsilon)\), \(|\epsilon|=1\), is unchanged.

statements.title: A comparison preserving the vacuum and its operations
statements.text: For nonzero-level Heisenberg modules over \(\mathbb C\), construct an independently defined comparison between negative-current coinvariants and the degreewise completed curved cochain transform on one common localized category, preserving the marked vacuum, translation, rational collision maps and logarithmic transport. Extend the Gaussian endpoint construction to nilpotent vacuum extensions with compatible transport and framing: for two unit charges at level three, increasing-normal-coordinate graph transport around a positive full turn gives \(e^{-2\pi i/3}\), whereas positive Fock continuation gives \(e^{2\pi i/3}\). An opposite-transport functor or a comparison with the reverse braided target remains to be constructed, together with the comparison preserving mixed operations of independent local bulk observables. The outgoing collision normalization is taken on the positive-real branch in this phase test.

statements.title: The raw-level curved point dual
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra with invariant form \(B\) normalized by long-root square two, and let \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\notin\mathbb Q\). For the universal affine algebra at raw level \(k\), the curved point dual is \((C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g((z))),d_{\mathrm{CE}},+\eta_k)\), where \(\eta_k(xz^m,yz^n)=kmB(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0}\) and \(d\alpha(x,y)=-\alpha([x,y])\). Complete separately in each exterior degree by finite subsets of \(z^{-1}\mathfrak g[z^{-1}]\), allowing finite \(\mathfrak g[[z]]\)-dual support separately for each such subset, with no product over exterior degrees. This is the point dual for the universal envelope, rather than a formula for simple quotients or an identification with the affine vertex algebra at the complementary level.

statements.title: KZ fusion with an explicit collision comparison
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), long-root square two and \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\notin\mathbb Q\), induce \(\mathbb V^k(E)\) from finite-dimensional \(\mathfrak g\)-modules \(E\), with positive currents acting trivially on the top. Their fixed-level product is \(\mathbb V^k(E)\odot\mathbb V^k(F)=\mathbb V^k(E\otimes F)\), with energy completion \(\prod_hX_{[h]}\), associator \(\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}(-\Omega_{12}/\kappa,-\Omega_{23}/\kappa)\), and upper-half-plane vertex braiding \(\operatorname{flip}\,e^{\pi i\Omega/\kappa}\), where \(\Omega\) is the Casimir tensor of \(B\). The rational-current Chevalley–Eilenberg collision map from distinct points to the completed one-point product is a quasi-isomorphism on modules with a finite Weyl filtration and finite-dimensional tops. The comparison extends to bounded-above complexes in that exact category by completing each term before direct-sum totalization; the completed target need not itself have finite support.

statements.title: An affine endomorphism obstruction
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), use algebraic Laurent-polynomial \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) modes at any raw level \(k\), with \([e,f]=h\), \((e,f)=1\) and \((h,h)=2\), and put \(W_k=A_k\otimes_{U(z^{-1}\mathfrak{sl}_2[z^{-1}])}\mathbb C\). In full algebraic Chevalley–Eilenberg cochains computing ordinary \(\operatorname{RHom}_{A_k}(W_k,W_k)\), the degree-one cochain sending \(f_{-1}\) to the induced vacuum and every other negative basis mode to zero represents a nonzero class at every \(k\). Consequently this endomorphism dg algebra cannot be quasi-isomorphic to \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)^{\mathrm{op}}\) concentrated in degree zero, including at irrational shifted level. This assertion uses algebraic modes and full Hom; it does not replace the coinvariant construction of the KZ connection.

statements.title: A commutative noncritical vacuum model
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), with long roots of square two, and any \(k\ne-h^\vee\), let \(V^k(\mathfrak g)\) be the universal vacuum and use continuous finite-jet cochains. The inclusion \(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g[[z]];\mathbb C)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g[[z]];V^k(\mathfrak g))\) is a dg vertex quasi-isomorphism with commutative source, and vacuum self-Ext in discrete smooth modules is \(H^\bullet(\mathfrak g;\mathbb C)\). It supplies a commutative \(E_3\)-model; uniqueness among all \(E_3\)-structures with this cohomology holds for \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) but fails for general simple \(\mathfrak g\), already for \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\).

statements.title: The nonabelian physical comparison
statements.text: For complex simple \(\mathfrak g\) at noncritical level, construct the boundary-module functor from an independently defined Chern–Simons theory and compare its supported insertions with affine rational-current collision maps. The comparison must preserve the universal vacuum, level normalization, horizontal transport and mixed bulk/boundary operations. Extend the algebraic collision comparison beyond finite Weyl filtrations only after identifying a module category and completion on which all iterated products are defined.

statements.title: Noncritical rational fusion and resonance
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra with long-root square two, \(k\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\kappa=k+h^\vee\ne0\). On finitely generated smooth universal-affine modules locally finite under \(\mathfrak g[[z]]\), with their Sugawara grading-restricted generalized module structure, the rational-current fusion product represents the Huang–Lepowsky–Zhang \(P(z)\)-intertwining maps for \(z\ne0\). For finite-dimensional Weyl tops, its associator and braiding are obtained by reducing the KZ operators on formal fusion lattices over \(\mathbb C[[\varepsilon]]\) at \(\kappa+\varepsilon\); direct evaluation is valid when constituent conformal weights have no nonzero integral differences in each pairwise and triple top tensor product. Resonant lattices can be nonstandard, so an unqualified substitution into a generic KZ matrix is insufficient.

The comparison must identify the parameter, associator, braiding and quotient maps. Admissible and negative-rational simple quotients require separate choices of category and recipient; an ordinary strong monoidal fibre to vector spaces is not assumed.

statements.title: Criticality does not remove curvature
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(\mathfrak g\ne0\) be finite-dimensional and simple, with invariant form \(B\) normalized by long-root square two, and take its universal untwisted affine algebra at \(k=-h^\vee\), without a degree derivation. Its curved point dual is \((C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathfrak g((z))),d_{\mathrm{CE}},\eta_{-h^\vee})\), where \(\eta_k(xz^m,yz^n)=kmB(x,y)\delta_{m+n,0}\); completion is separately by finite negative-mode subsets in each exterior degree, with finite positive support for each subset and no product over exterior degrees. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), normalized by \(B(h,h)=2\), the commuting pair \(hz,hz^{-1}\) has curvature \(-4\), so this cocycle is not exact. The vanishing shifted level \(k+h^\vee=0\) therefore supplies no uncurving of this model.

statements.title: Self-duality without a compact Serre functor
statements.text: For a nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), use discrete smooth modules of its untwisted affine algebra at \(k=-h^\vee\), without a degree derivation. Let \(\mathcal C\) be the idempotent-complete thick dg subcategory of the ordinary derived category generated by algebraic inductions from finite-dimensional smooth representations of central inverse images of compact open Lie subalgebras, and let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)\). There is no functor \(S:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\) with natural complex-linear isomorphisms \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)^*\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,SA)\), where Hom means degree-zero derived Hom and the star is the full algebraic dual. Nevertheless \(\mathcal S^\vee\simeq\mathcal S\) as presentable dg categories under the semi-infinite pairing.

statements.title: Critical vacuum self-extensions
statements.text: For a finite-dimensional simple complex \(\mathfrak g\), normalized by long-root square two, let \(V^{-h^\vee}\) be the universal affine vacuum in the category of discrete smooth fixed-level modules. Writing \(Z=\mathcal O(\operatorname{Op}_{{}^LG}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[[z]]))\) for its regular-disc oper centre, one has \(\operatorname{Ext}^\bullet(V^{-h^\vee},V^{-h^\vee})\cong\Omega_Z^\bullet\otimes H^\bullet(\mathfrak g;\mathbb C)\); the constant-\(\mathfrak g\)-relative version omits the last factor. The differential from first-order variation of the level acts as \(d_{\mathrm{dR}}\otimes1\).

statements.title: The universal curved Virasoro dual
statements.text: For the universal Virasoro algebra over \(\mathbb C\) at any \(c\in\mathbb C\), use \(\mathfrak w=\mathbb C((z))\partial_z\), positive polarization \(P=\prod_{n\ge-1}\mathbb CL_n\), and negative modes \(D=\bigoplus_{n\le-2}\mathbb CL_n\). Its point dual is the curved continuous Chevalley–Eilenberg algebra \((B_c,d,\Omega_c)\), where \(d\alpha(x,y)=-\alpha([x,y])\) and \(\Omega_c(L_m,L_n)=c(m^3-m)\delta_{m+n,0}/12\). In degree \(q\), \(B_c\) is a product over finite negative-mode subsets of size at most \(q\), with finite positive-dual support separately in every factor; there is no product over exterior degrees. This computation is for the universal envelope and does not supply the curved dual of a simple quotient.

statements.title: A charge-independent universal vacuum model
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for every complex \(c\), let \(\mathrm{Vir}_c\) be the universal vacuum and \(W_1=\prod_{m\ge-1}\mathbb CL_m\) the formal regular-vector-field algebra. On continuous finite-jet cochains, the inclusion \(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(W_1;\mathbb C)\hookrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(W_1;\mathrm{Vir}_c)\) is a central, commutative dg vertex quasi-isomorphism. Universal vacuum self-Ext in discrete smooth modules is \(\Lambda(\omega_3)\), \(|\omega_3|=3\), and this supplies a strictly unital commutative \(E_3\)-model whose Browder bracket vanishes. Identifying this model with geometric mixed bulk/boundary operations is a separate open comparison.

statements.title: Minimal models and a finite weak Hopf algebra
statements.text: For coprime integers \(2\le p<q\), put \(c_{p,q}=1-6(p-q)^2/(pq)\), and take finite direct sums of ordinary simple modules of the simple Virasoro vertex algebra \(L(c_{p,q},0)\) over \(\mathbb C\). The output constructed from full rational Ward invariants at distinct points agrees with the vertex \(P(z)\)-tensor product, with common continuation paths and the simple vacuum as unit. If \(I\) indexes the simple modules, the exact faithful long bimodule fibre \(F(M)=\bigoplus_{i,j\in I}\operatorname{Hom}(L_i,M\boxtimes L_j)\) takes values in \(\mathbb C^I\)-bimodules and reconstructs a finite weak Hopf algebra whose finite module category has the same ribbon structure. Its tensor unit projector is \(\Delta(1)\), and its scalar counit need not be a character; this statement concerns the finite simple-quotient category, not all modules of rational central charge.

statements.title: Singular sewing requires full radical descent
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), take \(b\ne0\), \(b^2\notin\mathbb Q\), \(c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2\), and \(h_{r,s}=((b+b^{-1})^2-(rb+s/b)^2)/4\), with \(r,s\ge1\). For fixed external weights and two coefficient-one three-point Ward forms, if both forms annihilate the entire radical of \(M(c,h_{r,s})\), the Verma block limit as the intermediate weight tends to \(h_{r,s}\) exists coefficient by coefficient and equals sewing through the simple quotient. At each descendant level every positive Smith exponent of the Gram family is one; this is the transversality that makes the conclusion follow from descent. At \(c=1\), intermediate weight \(1/4\) and four fixed external weights \(1/16\), both forms descend at every level but the level-two Verma limit exceeds the quotient coefficient by \(1/768\), so the irrational theorem cannot be specialized without an additional condition.

statements.title: Formal Beltrami sources and Ward insertions
statements.text: For the universal Virasoro vacuum over \(\mathbb C\) at any \(c\), let \(\mu\) be a formal series with zero constant term in finitely many commuting parameters, with smooth compactly supported coefficients on a planar sphere chart. With \(\bar\partial(z-w)^{-1}=\pi\delta^2(z-w)\), source coupling \(-\pi^{-1}\int\mu T\,d^2z\), and \(f_\mu\) normalized by \(\bar\partial f_\mu=\mu f_\mu'\), \(f_\mu=z+O(z^{-1})\), the normalized vacuum functional \(Z_c=e^{W_c}\) satisfies \(-\pi\delta W_c/\delta\mu=(c/12)\operatorname{Sch}(f_\mu)\) and \(W_c[0]=0\). Nested annular mode insertions with zero/one cutoff plateaux recover the ordered vacuum matrix coefficients, and the punctured-flow identity determines the contact terms for overlapping cutoffs; other plateau values require weighted residues. These are identities of continuous formal source coefficients, with no assertion of convergence in \(\mu\).

statements.title: Continuous represented fusion and five-point sewing
statements.text: For every real \(c>1\), with positive principal labels \(P\) and highest weights \(h_P=(c-1)/24+P^2\), construct a category of completed complex Virasoro representations whose product represents the trivalent Ward maps. Its input domains must be preserved when one trivalent output is inserted into another input, with absolute control of descendant sums and internal-momentum integrals on a common nonempty configuration domain. Prove the channel comparison for five independently variable positive principal labels and identify it with the label-space pentagon; a fifth vacuum stress insertion and scalar four-point transforms have narrower scope.

statements.title: Finite vacuum models and exterior algebras
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra of rank \(r\), with exponents \(m_i\), and let \(V=W^k(\mathfrak g)\) be its universal principal \(W\)-algebra, retaining the universal generators at special levels. In the category \(\mathcal S_k\) of all weak modules, at every noncritical level \(k\ne-h^\vee\), absolute \(\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal S_k}(V,V)\) is computed by a bounded finite-dimensional conformal-weight-zero complex and has Euler characteristic zero. Outside a finite rational set of noncritical levels, it is \(\Lambda_{\mathbb C}(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r)\), with \(|\eta_i|=2m_i+1\), and the associative derived endomorphism algebra is \(A_\infty\)-formal, in particular for every \(k\notin\mathbb Q\). For \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) and \(\mathfrak{so}_5\), the exterior answer and formality hold at every noncritical level, respectively as \(\Lambda(\eta_3,\eta_5)\) and \(\Lambda(\eta_3,\eta_7)\); the \(\mathfrak{sl}_3\) result includes \(k=-12/5,-4/3\), where \(c=-22/5\).

statements.title: Exceptional universal \(W_4\) self-extensions
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(V=W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_4)\) be universal, with \(\tau=k+4\in\{3/2,-3/2,2/3,-2/3\}\), and take absolute Ext in all weak modules. Its Poincaré polynomial is \(1+t^3+t^5+t^7+2t^8+t^9+t^{10}+t^{11}+2t^{12}+t^{15}\), so its total dimension is twelve. Nonzero generators of the degree-three, degree-five and degree-seven spaces satisfy \(\eta_3\eta_5\ne0\), \(\eta_3\eta_7\ne0\) and \(\eta_5\eta_7=0\); at \(\tau=\pm3/2\), the canonical Drinfeld–Sokolov map \(\Lambda(\theta_3,\theta_5,\theta_7)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}(V,V)\) has kernel \((\theta_5\theta_7)\). Multiplication involving the additional classes and associative formality at these levels remain open.

statements.title: A curved bar construction for all weak \(W_3\)-modules
statements.text: For every \(c\in\mathbb C\), let \(V_c\) be the regular universal \(W_3\)-algebra, let \(A_c\) be the closure of its finite mode operations for pointwise convergence on discrete cyclic weak modules, and set \(e(a)=\pi_0(a\mathbf1)\), \(E=\ker e\), where \(\pi_0\) projects onto the vacuum-weight line. The curved bar algebra \(\widehat B=\prod_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E^{\otimes n},\mathbb C)\), with algebraic tensors, the topology annihilating finite-dimensional finite-length tensor spaces, graded-opposite bar multiplication and curvature \(h(a,b)=e(ab)\), has free contramodules \(B[[M]]^r=\prod_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E^{\otimes n},M^{r-n})\); twisting gives a dg adjunction \(K\dashv F\) for possibly unbounded smooth complexes, with \(F(Q)^r=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(A_c,Q^r_{\mathrm{disc}})\). Curved contramodules free on degree-zero generators \(M\), with every recovered orbit map \(a\mapsto e(a)m+(Dm)(a-e(a)1)\) continuous into discrete \(M\), form an abelian category exactly equivalent to all weak \(V_c\)-modules. For ordinary weak modules, bar cochains continuous successively in the mode inputs, with each intermediate Hom space treated as discrete, compute derived Hom and Yoneda composition.
statements.antecedents: Beilinson (2007); De Sole–Kac (2005); Al-Ali–Linshaw (2016); Positselski (2009); Clarke–Crossley–Whitehouse (2006); Bousfield (2003); Damiolini–Gibney–Tarasca (2019).

statements.title: Braided quantum Hamiltonian reduction
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a simple complex Lie algebra of type \(A,D\) or \(E\), let \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\), and let \(f\in\mathfrak g\) be any nilpotent element. Quantum Hamiltonian reduction \(H_f^0\) is a braided tensor equivalence between the category of finite direct sums of affine Weyl modules \(\mathbb V^k_\lambda\), induced from finite-dimensional simple \(\mathfrak g\)-modules of dominant integral highest weight \(\lambda\), and the category of finite direct sums of their reductions as \(W^k(\mathfrak g,f)\)-modules. The reduced category is rigid, with \(H_f^0(\mathbb V^k_{\lambda^*})\) dual to \(H_f^0(\mathbb V^k_\lambda)\), where \(\lambda^*\) labels the dual finite-dimensional representation.
statements.cite: Creutzig–Dhillon–Nakatsuka, [The Kazhdan–Lusztig category of W-algebras of simply-laced Lie algebras at irrational levels](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.04667) (2026), Theorems 1.1 and 5.2; §§2.1–2.2.

statements.title: Nonlinear derived duality and exceptional products
statements.text: For universal principal \(W_3\) and \(W_4\) over \(\mathbb C\), construct a polarized completed curved dual, define the null classes on smooth complexes and contramodules, and prove that the twisting adjunction induces an equivalence after localization. The comparison must preserve the vacuum and intertwine quantum Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction; its extension to rational simple quotients remains a separate question. For \(W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_4)\) with \(k+4=\pm3/2,\pm2/3\), determine the remaining products, associative formality and the orders of the two local torsion summands.

statements.title: The RTT ghost dual vacuum
statements.text: For the crossing-normalized RTT double of \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) over \(\mathbb C\), \(n\ge2\), with arbitrary central level \(K\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\) and no determinant-one quotient, use torsion-free weight-graded lattices complete separately in each weight, with finite-dimensional classical weight spaces vanishing below weight zero, and take the \(\hbar\)-adic completion for vertex operations. Its dual vacuum has odd generators \(c_{ij,s}\) of cohomological degree one and weight \(s-1\), with \(c(y)=\sum_{s\ge1}c_sy^{s-1}\), \(dc(y)=-c(y)^2\), \(Tc_s=sc_{s+1}\), and \[c_{ij}(y)c_{kl}(y')+c_{kl}(y')c_{ij}(y)=\frac{\hbar}{y-y'}\bigl(c_{kj}(y)-c_{kj}(y')\bigr)\bigl(c_{il}(y)-c_{il}(y')\bigr).\] Ordered exterior monomials give a topological basis, and the fields \(Y(a,z)b=(e^{zT}a)b\) have a unique unitary, translation-covariant exchange compatible with the differential, the Yang–Baxter equation and both hexagons. Its coefficient of \(\hbar^j\) on homogeneous inputs \(a,b\) has pole order at most \(j+\operatorname{wt}(a)+\operatorname{wt}(b)\).

statements.title: Monoidal Koszul cochains and spectral fusion
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for the normalized \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) Yangian with \(n\ge2\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\) and no determinant-one quotient, let \(M,N\) be torsion-free weightwise complete lattices whose classical weight spaces are finite-dimensional and vanish below weight zero. If \(B\) is the RTT ghost dual vacuum and \(K(M)\) denotes restricted graded Koszul cochains with coefficients in \(M\), the dressed left \(B\)-action and the coaction cup product give \(K(M)\widehat\otimes_BK(N)\simeq K(M\widehat\otimes N)\). With \(\sigma_zT^*(u)=T^*(u-z)\), the coproduct \(\Delta_z=(\sigma_z\otimes1)\Delta\) satisfies \((\Delta_x\otimes1)\Delta_y=(1\otimes\Delta_y)\Delta_{x+y}\) on the rational representatives before their Laurent expansions at separated spectral points. The central coproduct adds boundary levels, and the fundamental intertwiner \(1-\hbar P/(y-y')\) becomes invertible after spectral localization; at numerical \(\hbar\), this requires \(y-y'\ne0\) and \((y-y')^2\ne\hbar^2\).

statements.title: Noncritical graded vacuum cohomology
statements.text: Let \(V_K\) be the universal normalized RTT vacuum of \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) over \(\mathbb C\), \(n\ge2\), with \(K\ne-n\), formal \(\hbar\) of weight \(-1\), no determinant-one quotient and scalar affine form \(\kappa_K(X,Y)=K(\operatorname{tr}(XY)-\operatorname{tr}(X)\operatorname{tr}(Y)/n)\). In the category of torsion-free weightwise complete graded lattices bounded below and of finite type, the one-vacuum Koszul complex is a dg \(\hbar\)-adic quantum vertex superalgebra whose cohomology is torsion-free and has topological basis \[\mathbb C[d_r:r\ge0]\otimes\Lambda(\lambda_s:s\ge2)\otimes H^*(\mathfrak{gl}_n;\mathbb C).\] Here \(\sum_{r\ge0}d_rv^r=(1-\operatorname{qdet}T(v))/\hbar\), \(\lambda_s=\operatorname{tr}c_s\), and \(H^*(\mathfrak{gl}_n)=\Lambda(\eta_1,\eta_3,\ldots,\eta_{2n-1})\), with \(\eta_1=\lambda_1\). The cohomology fields are regular and supercommutative, with \(Td_r=(r+1)d_{r+1}\) and \(T\lambda_s=s\lambda_{s+1}\).

statements.title: Smooth quantum duality
statements.text: For the normalized \(\mathfrak{gl}_n\) Yang double, \(n\ge2\), over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^N)\), construct twisting and coinduction functors between smooth modules and curved contramodules that satisfy the curvature, Leibniz and adjunction identities, and prove an equivalence in explicitly defined derived localizations. Establish compatibility as \(N\) varies before passing to a formal limit. Separately, construct fixed-level boundary collision products and compare them with the level-additive central coproduct.

statements.title: Scalar trigonometric fields
statements.text: Put \(P=\mathbb C[x_0,x_1,\ldots]\), \(Tx_r=x_{r+1}\), and \(V=P[[\hbar]]\), completed only in \(\hbar\). The Wick extension of the contraction \(\hbar/(e^u-1)\), with \(J=x_0\) and \(Y(J,u)J=(e^{uT}J)J+\hbar/(e^u-1)\), gives a quantum vertex algebra with field target \(P((u))[[\hbar]]\) and exchange target \((P\otimes P\otimes\mathbb C[q,q^{-1},(q-1)^{-1}])[[\hbar]]\), where \(q=e^u\). Locality is uniform in the spectator at each finite \(\hbar\)-precision, and the exchange satisfies unitarity, Yang–Baxter and both hexagons. There is no uniform pole bound for complete inputs: the exchange of \(\sum_{r\ge0}\hbar^rx_r\) with \(J\) has poles of unbounded order.

statements.title: A completion obstruction to an algebraic polar target
statements.text: Let \(k\) have characteristic zero, \(R=k[[\hbar]]\), let \(V\) be a separated complete flat \(R\)-module, and let \(T\) be an \(R\)-linear endomorphism. If an \(R\)-linear exchange map on \(V\otimes_RV\) takes values in the strictly algebraic target \((V\otimes_RV)\otimes_RR[q,q^{-1},(q-1)^{-1}]\) and satisfies \([T_1,S]=-q\partial_qS\), every output is regular at \(q=1\). A singular exchange on such a complete state module therefore requires a larger target, such as a completion that permits the pole order to grow with \(\hbar\)-precision.

statements.title: Meromorphic Yangian–quantum-loop comparison
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be complex semisimple, \(\hbar\notin\mathbb Q\), \(q=e^{\pi i\hbar}\), and \(|q|\ne1\). On finite-dimensional noncongruent Yangian modules, whose poles of each root current \(x_i^\pm(u)\) have no nonzero integral differences, the functor \(\Gamma\) to quantum-loop modules has coherent meromorphic tensorators for the deformed Drinfeld coproducts and preserves the braidings from the commutative parts \(R^0\) of the universal R-matrices. If \(\Pi\subset\mathbb C\) satisfies \((\Pi-\Pi)\cap\mathbb Z=\{0\}\) and \(\Pi\pm\hbar/2\subset\Pi\), then \(\Gamma\) restricts to an equivalence between the finite-dimensional module subcategories whose root-current, Cartan-current and inverse-Cartan-current poles lie respectively in \(\Pi\) and \(\exp(2\pi i\Pi)\), with the meromorphic tensor comparison wherever the shifted products are defined.
statements.cite: Gautam–Toledano Laredo, [Meromorphic tensor equivalence for Yangians and quantum loop algebras](https://arxiv.org/html/1403.5251v6), Publications Mathématiques de l’IHÉS 125 (2017), 267–337, §§2.5–2.6, 6.2–6.5.

Comparing with an elliptic quantum vertex algebra requires identifying its classical state space and its elliptic modulus throughout the deformation.

statements.title: Scalar bar–cobar duality and wheel defects
statements.text: Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic zero, \(G=\mathbb G_a\) or \(\mathbb G_m\), \(\varepsilon=\pm1\), and \(0\ne\gamma\in\mathcal O(G^2)\), with no nonunit factor depending on only one variable; write \(O_m=\mathcal O(G^m)\), \(\Lambda_m=O_m^{S_m}\), and let a superscript \(S_m,\varepsilon\) mean transformation by \(\varepsilon^{\ell(w)}\), with \(\ell(w)\) the Coxeter length. The coalgebra \(C_{\gamma,m}=(\prod_{i<j}\gamma(Z_i,Z_j))O_m^{S_m,\varepsilon}\), with consecutive-block coproducts, and the quadratic algebra \(B_\gamma=T_k(O_1)/(\gamma O_2^{S_2,\varepsilon})\), with generators in degree one, satisfy \(\Omega C_\gamma\simeq B_\gamma\) and \(C_\gamma\simeq\operatorname{Bar}B_\gamma\) in the category of sequences of \(\Lambda_m\)-modules. If also \(\gamma(Z_1,Z_2)\) and \(\gamma(Z_2,Z_1)\) are coprime, the map from \(B_{\gamma,m}\) to the big shuffle space \(O_m^{S_m,-\varepsilon}\), with unaveraged shuffle kernel \(\gamma(Z_j,Z_i)\) and permutation sign \((-\varepsilon)^{\ell(w)}\), has kernel \(H^0_{W_m}(B_{\gamma,m})\) and cokernel \(H^1_{W_m}(B_{\gamma,m})\), where \(W_m\subset\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda_m\) is the wheel locus. Its image is the shuffle subalgebra generated in weight one, so the map to that smaller algebra is surjective with the same torsion kernel and zero cokernel.
statements.antecedents: Bayer–Sturmfels (1998); Loday–Vallette (2012); Kunin–Lienkaemper–Rosen (2020); Dotsenko–Feigin–Reineke (2021); Dotsenko–Feigin–Kucharski–Reineke (2024); Neguţ (2022).

statements.title: When wheel defects appear
statements.text: Over a field \(k\) of characteristic zero, let \(\gamma\) be a unit times \(g(Z_1-Z_2)\) on \(\mathbb G_a\), or a unit times \(g(Z_1/Z_2)\) on \(\mathbb G_m\), where \(g\ne0\), \(g(0)\ne0\) in the multiplicative case, and \(\gamma(Z_1,Z_2)\) is coprime to its reverse; either exchange sign \(\varepsilon=\pm1\) is allowed. Over an algebraic closure, let \(r\) be the least length of a root sequence of \(g\), with repetitions allowed, whose sum is zero in the additive case or whose product is one in the multiplicative case; set \(r=\infty\) if there is none. Then \(r\ge3\), both wheel-supported defects of the quadratic-to-shuffle comparison vanish in weights \(m<r\), and both are nonzero in every weight \(m\ge r\). If \(r<\infty\), the weight-one-generated shuffle algebra is neither quadratic nor Koszul for its weight grading.

statements.title: One-loop Hall currents and their coproduct
statements.text: Over \(R=\mathbb Q[\eta]\), take the zero-potential one-loop Hall algebra \(B=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]^{S_n}\), with loop weight \(-\eta\), first input the subrepresentation, no rank shift and unaveraged shuffle kernel \((v+\eta)/v\). Its Cartan extension \(A=B\rtimes R[p_0,p_1,\ldots]\), where \(p_r\) acts on weight \(n\) by multiplication by \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^r\), is faithfully realized by rational creation and occupation currents over the family of all finite sets of algebraically independent sites. Cartan dressing gives a unital algebra map \(\Delta_z:A\to(A\otimes_RA)((z^{-1}))\), conjugate to separation of the sites, with \((\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta_z=\mathrm{id}\), \((1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta_z=e^{zT}\) and shifted coassociativity: for three blocks at \((x+z+w,y+w,t)\), compose rationally and then expand at \(w=\infty\), followed coefficientwise by \(z=\infty\). The comparison holds at \(\eta=0\) as well as at nonzero parameters, and joint faithfulness uses the whole family of finite site sets.

statements.title: Tree-level graded duality
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and \(\mathfrak a=\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with \(\epsilon\) even, so the second current tower is an abelian adjoint module. There is a graded algebraic identification \(B_{\mathrm{pol}}\simeq(\operatorname{Bar}U(\mathfrak a[t]))^{\vee_{\mathrm{fib},t}}\); cobar recovers \(U(\mathfrak a[t])\), whose primitives and \(d/dt\) recover the current conformal algebra and then \(V(\mathfrak a)\). The coefficients are polynomial in ghosts and jets; full energy-homogeneous coefficient cochains and completed smooth duals have different carriers.

statements.title: A flat quantum quotient in four twistor degrees
statements.text: Let \(\mathfrak g\) be finite-dimensional and simple over \(\mathbb C\), normalize its invariant form \(K\) by long-root squared length two, and choose \(a,\ell\in\mathbb C\) satisfying \(2a\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{ad}}((\operatorname{ad}X)^4)=3\ell^2K(X,X)^2\) for every \(X\in\mathfrak g\). Over \(R=\mathbb C[s]/(s^3)\), with \(e_1=(1,0)\), \(e_2=(0,1)\), retain currents \(J[0],J[e_1],J[e_2],J[e_1+e_2],\widetilde J[0]\) and axions \(E[e_1],E[e_2],E[e_1+e_2],F[0]\), assign \(J[\alpha],E[\alpha]\) twistor degree \(\alpha\) and \(\widetilde J[\alpha],F[\alpha]\) degree \(\alpha+e_1+e_2\), and kill every state of total degree outside \(\{0,e_1,e_2,e_1+e_2\}\). This quotient admits an \(R\)-free one-loop vertex deformation with quadratic current coefficient \(s^2a\), linear coefficients \(-s^2h^\vee a/3\), \(-2s^2h^\vee a/3\), axion coupling \(s\ell\), and an explicit differential ghost vertex algebra, both free on their retained ordered derivative monomials. Their pairing \(I\) satisfies \(QI+\tfrac12I_{(0)}I=D_{\mathrm{tot}}H\) for an explicit \(H\), so \(Q+I_{(0)}\) squares to zero on the ghost algebra tensored with every ordinary untwisted module of this quotient; the coupling is Maurer–Cartan modulo total translation.

Form the level-zero vacuum \(V=A\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}\mathbb C\) and co-vacuum \(W=A\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n)}\mathbb C\), inducing from the trivial modules, and compute derived Hom in all algebraic left \(A\)-modules with full algebraic cochains and product totalization. Then \(H^0\operatorname{REnd}_A(W)=U(\mathfrak a)^{\mathrm{op}}\), and \(\mathfrak a^*\) embeds as a split vector-space summand of \(H^1\operatorname{REnd}_A(W)\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{RHom}_A(W,V)=0\), whereas \(\mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(\mathfrak n)}V\simeq\mathbb C\).

statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(R=\mathbb C[v_1,v_2]\) with \(\{f,g\}=\partial_1f\,\partial_2g-\partial_2f\,\partial_1g\), and let \(\mathfrak a=(R,\{\ ,\ \})\otimes\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)\), with even \(\epsilon\) and both constant Hamiltonians retained. The universal level-zero current vertex algebra is \(V(\mathfrak a)=U(\mathfrak a[t,t^{-1}])\otimes_{U(\mathfrak a[t])}\mathbb C\); its polynomial ghost algebra is the dual of the homological Chevalley–Eilenberg coalgebra of \(\mathfrak a[t]\), restricted jointly by the shifted fibre degree \(\deg(v^\alpha)=\alpha-(1,1)\) and \(t\)-degree, and is quasi-isomorphic to the corresponding restricted dual of \(\operatorname{Bar}U(\mathfrak a[t])\). The cobar of that coalgebra recovers \(U(\mathfrak a[t])\), whose primitives and translation recover \(V(\mathfrak a)\).

statements.title: An obstruction beyond local cochains
statements.text: Let \(S=\mathbb C[v_1,v_2,z,z^{-1}]\) carry the Poisson bracket in \(v_1,v_2\), and give \(S\) its adjoint module structure over \(\mathfrak h=(S,\{\ ,\ \})\). With \(\mathrm{vol}=dv_1\wedge dv_2\wedge dz\), \(\partial^1=\partial_2\), \(\partial^2=-\partial_1\), and \(J_f=(\partial^a\partial_bf)\), define \(\iota_{\psi(f,g)}\mathrm{vol}=\operatorname{tr}(dJ_f\wedge dJ_g)\) and \(\Phi(f,Y)=\sum_{a,b=1}^2\partial_a\partial^b\bigl(Y(\partial^a\partial_bf)\bigr)\). The cocycle \(\Omega_H(f,g,h)=\Phi(f,\psi(g,h))+\Phi(g,\psi(h,f))+\Phi(h,\psi(f,g))\) represents a nonzero class in \(H^3(\mathfrak h;S)\) computed with all algebraic cochains. No algebraic two-cochain has differential equal to this cocycle.

statements.title: Polynomial Moyal cochains are not closed

At every fixed \(h\in\mathbb C^\times\), the finite-polynomial ghost dual is not preserved by the Chevalley–Eilenberg differential: the constant coefficient of \(b_h(v_1^{2r+1},v_2^{2r+1})\) is \((2r+1)!h^{2r}/2^{2r}\) for every \(r\ge0\). The homological Chevalley–Eilenberg coalgebra remains defined, and \(h\)-adic cochains provide the formal dual.

statements.title: The boundary algebra is a proper kernel
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), for every integer \(N\ge1\), let \(C_{\mathrm{fr}}\) be the polynomial relative \(\mathfrak{gl}_N\) BRST complex with adjoint and fundamental symplectic bosons and fundamental fermions at numerical \(\hbar=1\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be the corresponding Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex sheaf on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\). Put \(K_N=H^0(C_{\mathrm{fr}})\) and \(V_N=\Gamma(M_N,\mathcal D)_{\mathrm{fin}}/(\hbar-1)\), taking the torus-finite part before specialization, and write \(\chi^-=\phi\gamma\) for the invariant contraction of a fundamental fermion with a fundamental symplectic boson. The natural map identifies \(K_N\) with \(\ker(\chi^-_{(0)}:V_N\to V_N)\), and \(V_N=K_N\oplus\tau_{(-1)}K_N\) as graded vector spaces, where \(\tau\) is an odd global section of conformal weight zero with \(\chi^-_{(0)}\tau=N\).

statements.title: The sharp formal cohomology range

For each of \(\mathcal D\), every quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar^m\mathcal D\) with integer \(m\ge1\), and the classical quotient \(\mathcal D/\hbar\mathcal D\), its sheaf cohomology is nonzero exactly in degrees \(0\le k<N\). These groups are taken before numerical specialization.

statements.title: An exact determinant-torsion algebra
statements.text: For \(N\ge2\), on \(M_N=\operatorname{Hilb}^N(\mathbb C^2)\), let \(\mathcal D\) be the Arakawa–Kuwabara–Möller formal vertex sheaf over \(R=\mathbb C[[\hbar]]\), let \(\beta\) be the connecting map for \(0\to\mathcal D\xrightarrow{\hbar}\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/\hbar\mathcal D\to0\), and put \(\kappa_r=T^r\beta(\phi\psi)\), where \(\phi\psi\) is the classical invariant contraction of the two fundamental fermions. The normal-cup subalgebra generated by the scalar vacuum and the \(\kappa_r\), using finite sums and finite products, is \[\frac{R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Lambda(e_0,e_1,\ldots)}{(\hbar e_r\ (r\ge0),\ \Lambda^{\ge N})},\qquad e_r\mapsto\kappa_r.\] Each \(e_r\) has sheaf degree one, intrinsic even parity and conformal weight \(r+1\); the exterior sign comes from sheaf degree, and there is no completion in the translation index. Every nonempty increasing product of fewer than \(N\) generators is nonzero and not \(\hbar\)-divisible, remains nonzero in every finite \(\hbar\)-quotient, and vanishes under torus-finite specialization at \(\hbar=1\).

statements.title: A finite-rank obstruction to derived sewing
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), with algebraic tensor products and ordinary derived functors, fix \(\hbar\ne0\) and \(N\ge1\), let \(W=\mathbb C\langle x,y\rangle/(xy-yx-\hbar)\), \(\mathfrak g=W^{\mathrm{Lie}}\), \(U_N=U(\mathfrak g)/(z-N1)\), where \(z\) denotes the central Lie element \(1_W\), and \(A_N=(W^{\otimes N})^{S_N}\). For the algebraic power-sum map \(U_N\to A_N\), \(J(f)\mapsto\sum_i f^{(i)}\), the multiplication \(A_N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U_N}A_N\to A_N\) is never a quasi-isomorphism. The module \(F_N=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_N]^{S_N}\), with \(y_i=-\hbar\partial_{x_i}\), has no flat first-order lift as the central value varies from \(N\), and its resulting class in \(\operatorname{Ext}^2_{U_N}(F_N,F_N)\) is nonzero. For \(N=1,2\), \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_1(A_N,A_N)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Tor}^{U_N}_2(A_N,A_N)\ne0\), with the central-extension cap product surjecting onto \(A_N\); for \(N\ge3\), at least one of these two Tor groups is nonzero.

statements.text: Fix real \(c>1\), \(Q=\sqrt{(c-1)/6}\), principal weights \(h(P)=Q^2/4+P^2\) with \(P>0\), and normalized Virasoro sphere blocks \(F_p^s(x)\), \(F_p^t(x)\). statements.title: Boundary traces and the vacuum weight
statements.text: Fix real \(c>1\) and assume two positive principal Virasoro actions of weights \(h(P)=(c-1)/24+P^2\) are realized on \(L^2(\mathbb R_+,dP;\operatorname{HS}(\mathcal F))\), where \(\mathcal F\) is the oscillator Fock Hilbert space and the actions are \(L_n\xi=\pi_P(L_n)\xi\), \(\bar L_n\xi=\xi\pi_P(L_{-n})\), with their common finite-energy domain and trace-compatible positive sewing. Their faithful all-temperature state data are parametrized by measurable \(w>0\) almost everywhere with \(\int_0^\infty w(P)e^{-\beta P^2}\,dP<\infty\) for every \(\beta>0\), and have caps \(\Psi^w_\beta(P)=\sqrt{w(P)}e^{-\beta H_P/2}\), where \(H_P=P^2+N-1/24\) and \(N\) is the oscillator number operator on \(\mathcal F\). The Ward identities leave \(w\) free, while equality of the amplitude with the normalized modular vacuum amplitude at every temperature selects \(w=\rho_0\) almost everywhere. Here \(\rho_0(P)=2\sqrt2[\cosh(2\pi QP)-\cosh(2\pi\widehat QP)]\), \(Q=\sqrt{(c-1)/6}\), \(\widehat Q^2=Q^2-4\).

statements.title: A continuous spectral dual retaining multiplicities
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(S_{00}=\{\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)^{\mathrm{even}}:\phi(0)=\int\phi=0\}\) with its Schwartz topology, let \(E_n=\{f:e^{n\sqrt{1+x^2}}f\in H^n(\mathbb R)\}\) with norm \(\|e^{n\sqrt{1+x^2}}f\|_{H^n}\), and give \(E=\bigcap_{n\ge2}E_n\) its projective-limit Fréchet topology. The integer-summation map \(Z\phi(x)=2\sum_{m\ge1}\phi(me^x)\) is a continuous embedding with closed image, so the complex \([S_{00}\xrightarrow{Z}E]\), in degrees zero and one, has only \(H^1=M=E/Z(S_{00})\). For \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\), let \(m_\rho\) be the order of its zero \(\rho\) and set \(V_n=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{x^ke^{\rho x}/k!:0\le k<m_\rho\}}^{\,E_n'}\); the strong continuous dual of \(M\), twisted by the dilation character \(e^t\), is topologically \((\operatorname{ind\,lim}_nV_n)\otimes\mathbb C(1)\), with nondegenerate evaluation pairing into the character line \(\mathbb C(1)\). For the dilation generator \(\Theta_M[f]=[-f']\), each zero contributes its full Jordan block of length \(m_\rho\); neither the Riemann hypothesis nor simplicity of zeros is assumed.

statements.title: Integral arithmetic translations retain normal directions
statements.text: Fix a prime \(p\), a depth \(r\ge1\), and the category of \(p\)-complete, \(p\)-torsion-free \(\delta\)-algebras over \(\mathbb Z_p\), with Frobenius equal to the identity on \(\mathbb Z_p\); all completions below are \(p\)-adic, and profinite labels are interpreted through the constant profinite formal scheme, allowing variation on idempotent components. Put \(R=\mathbb Z_p[x_0,x_1,\ldots]^\wedge_p\), \(\varphi(x_i)=x_i^p+px_{i+1}\), and \(H_r=(\Gamma_{\mathbb Z_p}(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-2})\otimes\mathbb Z_p[w_0,w_1,\ldots])^\wedge_p\), where \(\Gamma\) denotes a divided-power algebra, its generator list is empty at \(r=1\), and \(H_r\) represents on each test algebra \(T\) displacements \(v\) satisfying \(\delta^i(v)\in pT\) for \(i<r\), with \(\delta^i(v)=pt_i\) and \(t_{r-1}=w_0\). Writing \(C(\mathbb Z_p,\mathbb Z_p)\) for continuous functions, the map \(R\hookrightarrow C(\mathbb Z_p,\mathbb Z_p)\widehat\otimes H_r\), \(f\mapsto[(a,v)\mapsto f(a+v)]\), is injective and intertwines finite-weight normal convolution; it extends to comparison maps of the entire congruence-groupoid nerve, whose enriched objects are \((a,v)\) and arrows exist when \(a\equiv b\pmod{p^r}\), compatibly with every composition, depth reduction and coefficient reduction, with Frobenius compatibility after twisting the source action by \(\varphi\). For \(r\ge2\), the relation \(\varphi(x_0)-x_0\) vanishes on arithmetic points but its normal coefficient \([t_0]\) is \(-p\), so point evaluation cannot retain this action modulo \(p^2\).

statements.title: Strong orientation on two compact component classes
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(S\) be a smooth projective Kummer K3 surface, \(E\) an elliptic curve and \(X=S\times E\), with a fixed Calabi–Yau volume form and induced trivial spin structure; choose a smooth elliptic fibre \(C\subset S\), a divisor \(D\) with \(D\cdot C=1\), points \(p\in C\), \(x\in E\), and \(L\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(E)\). In the actual component group \(K_0^{\mathrm{semi}}(X)\) of perfect complexes, let \(\Gamma\) be generated by \(\alpha=[\mathcal O_C\boxtimes\mathcal O_x]\) and \(\beta=[\mathcal O_p\boxtimes L]\), and restrict a Joyce–Upmeier square root \(J_F^{\otimes2}\simeq\det R\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,F)\), compatible with direct sums and equipped with a square-compatible unit, to these components. Then \(\Gamma\simeq\mathbb Z^2\), its Euler pairing is zero, and \(J\) admits associative unital square-compatible maps \(J_F\otimes J_G\otimes\det R\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,G)\simeq J_{F\oplus G}\), extending to every actual finite ordered filtration whose successive quotient classes lie in \(\Gamma\), independently of binary parenthesization and compatibly with refinements. For the fixed root, enhancement classes form a two-element torsor under \(H^2(\Gamma,\mathbb F_2)\).

statements.title: The numerical reduced Igusa formula
statements.text: Let \(S\) be a smooth projective complex K3 surface, \(E\) an elliptic curve, \(\beta\ne0\) an effective integral curve class on \(S\), \(d\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and \(n\in\mathbb Z\); use reduced Donaldson–Thomas invariants of \(S\times E\) defined by the translation quotient with finite stabilizers, rational stabilizer weights and the Behrend-weighted sign convention. With \(c(a,b,m)=[q^ap^by^m]\chi_{10}(y,q,p)^{-1}\) for the product-normalized Igusa cusp form, the numerical identity is \[\mathrm{DT}^{S\times E,\mathrm{red}}_{n,(\beta,d)}=(-1)^{n+1}\sum_{\substack{r>0,\ r\mid n\\ \beta/r\ \mathrm{integral}}}\frac1r\,c\!\left(\frac{(\beta/r)^2}{2},d-1,\frac nr\right).\] This includes imprimitive \(\beta\) through the displayed divisor sum and determines numerical invariants, without determining the parity-resolved BPS spaces or their brackets.
statements.cite: Georg Oberdieck, “Multiple cover formulas for K3 geometries, wall-crossing, and Quot schemes”, Geometry & Topology 28 (2024), Theorem 1.5; Georg Oberdieck and Junliang Shen, “Reduced Donaldson–Thomas invariants and the ring of dual numbers”, Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society 118 (2019).

statements.title: Negative-current homology obstructs preservation of the tensor unit
statements.text: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(A=L_1(\mathfrak{psl}(2|2))\) be the simple affine boundary algebra with its even \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) factors at levels \(-1,+1\), let \(\mathfrak g=A_1\) be its weight-one current space, and let \(\mathfrak n_-=t^{-1}\mathfrak g[t^{-1}]\) act by the actual negative current modes. In the ordinary algebraic derived category, \(F_-(A)=\mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(\mathfrak n_-)}A\) has \(H_{0,0}=\mathbb C\) and \(H_{1,2}=\mathbb C^{24\mid24}\), with every other group of conformal weight at most two zero; the indices denote homological degree and conformal weight. Consequently \(F_-\) cannot be strong unital monoidal from a tensor category with unit \(A\) to complexes of vector spaces with their ordinary tensor product.

Its derived augmentation endomorphism algebra is formal and is \(U(\mathfrak l)\) with zero differential, where \(\mathfrak l\) has generators \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) of degree \(-1\), a central generator \(\tau\) of degree \(-2\), brackets \([\alpha,\beta]=-\tau\), \([\gamma,\gamma]=2\tau\), and all other generator brackets zero up to graded skewsymmetry. For both full Hom and internally graded Hom, \[R\operatorname{Hom}_{U(L_n)}(W_n,V_n)=0,\qquad \mathbb C\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{U(N_n)}\operatorname{Res}_{N_n}V_n\simeq\mathbb C.\] At \(\mathfrak g=0\), the derived Hom is \(\mathbb C\), so the nonzero hypothesis is essential.
